items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: I think his name was Demling... Demling, that was the guy's name. And he didn't want us to leave, he wanted to keep us over there

ctx.x: When you play a solo, what do you try to do?

Well, sometimes I take a solo and when they're playing, they're vamping me, see? And I'm playing this solo. I may take it up in 16ths, see? I may take it up in 16ths, play a whole note and use some 16ths with it. But I'm going to use 16ths in the place of it, but with the same melody, see? Just like you say. I may go. See, I'm going on with the melody right on, but I'm putting something in between there, see? See? See, I get on back on that part. I never stay in that part. See, I go away from it, see. Because if…

Really? Mr. Tavern? Yeah, it was a tavern. Oh man, that place was like the idea of a band from York. That man made money, I mean he made money, hand over fist. He wanted to keep us, but I don't know, it seemed like them fellas that he had, you know, working there, them guys, they would take the tips. A lot of them guys would steal the tips, you know, and what a little snotty thing, a man handed a dollar and he'd stick it in his pocket, you know. He didn't want us to leave though, he wanted us to, I think his name…
